text: An API is a defined way for one piece of software to ask another for data or for an action, without either side needing to know how the other one works inside. You just need to know the shape of the question it accepts, and the shape of the answer it gives back.

Every API call has the same three moving parts. The client sends a request. The server processes it. Then the server sends back a response. Checking a bank balance, posting a tweet, asking an AI model to write a paragraph — same three steps, every time.

Here's that pattern as an actual example. A client asks a weather API for Boston's forecast. The server does its work. The response comes back with the answer. Nothing more mysterious is happening under the hood of any API you'll ever call.

Here's why this is lesson one of this entire course. Every AI application you build talks to a provider's API using this exact pattern. When your app calls Claude or GPT, it's sending a request to a server you don't control and reading back a response. That is the real work of an AI application.
Client, request, server, response — that's the whole shape. Next lesson, we zoom into the specific style of API that dominates the web and nearly every AI provider: REST.
